dataset_source.title: Sampling the materials space for conventional superconducting compounds
dataset_source.attribution: Source data: Tiago F. T. Cerqueira, Antonio Sanna and Miguel A. L. Marques, Sampling the materials space for conventional superconducting compounds, Materials Cloud 2023.163 v1, DOI 10.24435/materialscloud:qv-bq, CC BY 4.0. This catalogue is a derived projection with additional source-state screening commentary.

scope: Previously private source-model screening is now published as unscored source-computed material-design hypotheses. Historical private-screening wording is retained as context. These predictions are new to this reviewed catalogue only; experimental confirmation, worldwide first discovery, formal RPS and human scientific review are not claimed.
source_tc_scope: Source isotropic Eliashberg Tc in K at mu*=0.1 is a model result, not experimental Tc. It is a separate source product and is not associated with an individual Gaussian width or a numerical uncertainty interval.
pairing_response_scope: Retained ten-width lambda contrasts and independent source Tc products support bounded source-model comparisons. Chemical, mass, volume, sampling, spin and SOC effects can co-change; no universal causal or error-bound interpretation is assigned.
risk_tag_scope: Attention labels support browsing. Element labels are not measured magnetic ground states, rejection criteria or calibrated potential scores; no label does not mean no risk.

candidate.prototype: Fm-3m B1/rock-salt MoH primitive two-site source with octahedral H, not the known P63/mmc NiAs MoH phase
candidate.prototype_evidence: Fm-3m B1/rock-salt MoH primitive two-site source with octahedral H, not the known P63/mmc NiAs MoH phase
candidate.support_meaning: Preliminary screened support within the stated source model. This ordinal level is not a probability, formal RPS score or human scientific review.
candidate.risk_summary: The known competing MoH phase is hexagonal NiAs/P63mmc, with high-pressure synthesis and ambient recovered measurements; known superconductivity in that phase is not this B1 source phase. FCC gamma MoH exists as a pressure/temperature phase prior, while source B1 is locally stable at Gamma and sampled path. H loss, competing hcp/metal+H2, anharmonicity and the omitted magnetic competition of Cr/Mn controls are substantive falsifiers. The source paper reports a near-hull B1 phase in a separate calculation, not an exact-state thermodynamic certificate. PdH is a retained higher-lambda control and experimental benchmark, not omitted.
candidate.ambient_scope: Both source SCFs converge, near-zero coarse forces/stress and bounded fine response are measured. Fine Fmax=0 eV/A, P=-0.319 GPa, full max stress=0.319 GPa. Gamma optical compression is positive beyond printing bound and sampled path has no signed negative values. All listed q outputs have JOBDONE/last response convergence and no routine errors. This supports a finite-grid local/metastable source model, not global hull or experimental synthesis.
candidate.route_response: Mo replaces Cr in the same rock-salt metal/H site motif; source cell volume rises 31.870%, Mo-H versus Cr-H rises 0.180451 A and the metal self-neighbor distance rises 0.255196 A. Direct lambda is 21.448–41.624% larger at all ten sigma values and separate Eli mu=.1 rises 15.560 to 17.312 K. This bounded configured-scalar coupled metal/network contrast does not prove real magnetic CrH is a weaker superconductor.
candidate.next_action: Compare B1 MoH with the same-composition NiAs competitor and an H-loss reaction at a common functional, while separately testing magnetic CrH/MnH and common sampling for the source paired response. Retained B1 local stability and coupling gain support the bounded source hypothesis; easy phase conversion, H loss or magnetic/method reversal opposes it.

seven_criteria.identity: Complete ordered CIF/literal coarse-fine input/Gamma periodic species-site association is numerically supported; source input geometry and full tensor/forces are retained. Export occupancy is a discrete computational convention; source experimental P/T/occupancy and actual compiled unit constant are unknown. Exact-version input defaults scope the configured neutral scalar spin1/noSOC model, not magnetic ground state.
seven_criteria.quantitative_route_response: Mo replaces Cr in the same rock-salt metal/H site motif; source cell volume rises 31.870%, Mo-H versus Cr-H rises 0.180451 A and the metal self-neighbor distance rises 0.255196 A. seven_criteria.pairing_relevance: Exact target and mapped control direct source lambda arrays have the same favorable sign at all ten common broadening tokens; omega_ln has explicit K units and separate Eli/McM mu=.1 tables remain independent. Same underlying q mesh is observed. The sensitivity range is not a physical error bound; sigma units, full-BZ convergence, experimental Tc and pure-geometry causality remain unknown. Literal method differences are declared confounds.
seven_criteria.ambient_feasibility: Both source SCFs converge, near-zero coarse forces/stress and bounded fine response are measured. Fine Fmax=0 eV/A, P=-0.319 GPa, full max stress=0.319 GPa. Gamma optical compression is positive beyond printing bound and sampled path has no signed negative values. All listed q outputs have JOBDONE/last response convergence and no routine errors. This supports a finite-grid local/metastable source model, not global hull or experimental synthesis.
seven_criteria.competition_and_coherence: The known competing MoH phase is hexagonal NiAs/P63mmc, with high-pressure synthesis and ambient recovered measurements; known superconductivity in that phase is not this B1 source phase. FCC gamma MoH exists as a pressure/temperature phase prior, while source B1 is locally stable at Gamma and sampled path. H loss, competing hcp/metal+H2, anharmonicity and the omitted magnetic competition of Cr/Mn controls are substantive falsifiers. seven_criteria.novelty: MoH chemistry and P63/mmc superconductivity are known. Dated 2026-10-07 B1/FCC MoH searches found phase/structure predictions and FCC gamma phase prior, but no experimental superconducting exact B1 source state. The object is an ordered B1 source-phase and matched metal substitution hypothesis new to the reviewed catalogue, not first discovery of MoH or inherited NiAs Tc.
